verdict.rationale: MoQ Relay's own docs say arbitrary non-media data (chat, game state, telemetry, control channels) travels over the same relays as audio/video via the moq-net / @moq/net libraries, and via custom tracks. GitHub also describes text chat as a core feature and the transport as delivering WebRTC-like latency. However, the data API reference itself is only linked, not shown, so its depth and any data-specific latency behaviour are unproven. Missing for 10: visible data-API reference content (message/track semantics, ordering and reliability options), measured latency for data tracks, and independent or hands-on corroboration of data exchange alongside media.

support.subject: As a developer, participants exchange low-latency arbitrary data in the session alongside audio and video, with a documented data API

citations.quote: Chat, game state, telemetry, and control channels over the same relays with [`moq-net`](/lib/rs/moq-net.html) or [`@moq/net`](/lib/js/net.html).
Extend the protocol with custom tracks for any live content.
Includes text chat as both an example and a core feature.
MoQ delivers WebRTC-like latency without the constraints of WebRTC.
